### Do I have to pay for commercial use? 

No. You are not required to pay for a commercial license, however if you are using Obsidian for work in an organization we encourage you to purchase a commercial license to keep Obsidian independent and 100% user-supported. Learn more.

### Can I buy Obsidian add-ons or licenses for someone else? 

Yes! You can purchase Obsidian Credit for friends, family, and coworkers. This credit can be used to pay for any Obsidian license or service. To get started, create an account and buy credit. You can then send it to the recipient via email or a shareable link. Learn more. 

### What is your refund policy? 

We offer full refunds within 7 days of purchase with no questions asked for Obsidian Sync and Publish. However, please note that Catalyst licenses, Commercial licenses, and Obsidian Credit are non-refundable. Learn more. 

### Do you store, access, or process user data? 

Obsidian is a private and secure space for your thoughts. You can use our apps without sharing any personal information, and your data is stored locally on your device, making it inaccessible to us. Additionally, our apps do not collect telemetry data, and we never sell user data.

If you choose to use Obsidian Sync, your data is secured with AES‑256 end-to-end encryption, preventing us from reading it. Learn more.

### Do you offer discounts for education, nonprofits, or other groups? 

Yes, we do! Students, faculty members, and nonprofit employees are eligible for a 40% discount on Obsidian Sync and Publish. We do not offer any other discounts or promotions. Learn more.

title: License Overview
text:
## Summary

### Free for everyone

Obsidian is free for all purposes, including personal, commercial, and non-profit use. To support our development and help keep Obsidian 100% user-supported, you can optionally purchase a Catalyst or Commercial license. The Catalyst license is for individuals and includes perks like early access to beta versions. The Commercial license allows organizations to be featured supporters on our website.

### Your personal information is not required

Downloading Obsidian does not require an account, and we do not collect your personal information. You only need an account for payments or add-on services, and you can permanently delete your account at any time.

### Your data is local

Your data is saved locally on your device and is not sent to our server. If you use Obsidian Publish or Obsidian Sync, we handle your data only as needed for those services. Publish data is hosted on our servers. Sync data is encrypted and inaccessible to our staff. Learn more about our approach to privacy and security.

...

## License types

Obsidian is free for everyone to use. We offer optional paid licenses to support our development and provide additional benefits.

### Free use

You can download and use Obsidian for free, forever, for any purpose including: 

- Personal use
- Commercial use
- Non-profit and charitable organizations
- Educational institutions
- Government departments and agencies

You can download and use Obsidian without creating an account.

### Commercial license

Commercial Licenses are optional licenses that help keep Obsidian 100% user-supported. They can be purchased on an annual basis to show your organization's support for independent software development.

### Catalyst license

Catalyst Licenses are special licenses that help keep Obsidian 100% user-supported while offering additional benefits, including early access to insider builds.

title: What Obsidian actually costs in 2026, the real numbers
text:
Obsidian’s own pricing and licence pages (checked 13 October 2026) lead with the part that is genuinely true: the core app costs nothing, for anyone, indefinitely, including a business using it for work. What sits below that headline, in smaller print, is that the two things most people eventually want from it – getting the same vault on a phone and a laptop, and putting a note online for someone else to read – are each paid separately.

## The core app: free, no account, no catch

“Free without limits. No sign-up required.” That is Obsidian’s own description, and it holds up. Desktop and mobile apps, unlimited notes, unlimited local storage, no watermark, no feature locked behind a trial. Everything is stored as plain Markdown files on your device, which is the whole basis of Obsidian’s pitch to people who don’t want their notes living inside someone else’s database.

The free plan has no equivalent of Notion’s block cap or a note-count ceiling. If you only ever use Obsidian on one device, this is the entire cost, forever.

## Sync: the plan most individual users actually pay for

The moment you want the same vault on your phone and your laptop, the free plan stops covering it. Obsidian doesn’t sync accounts by default. That’s a separate product called Obsidian Sync, at $4 a month per user billed annually, or $5 a month billed monthly. It covers syncing your vault across devices, end-to-end encryption, version history, the ability to collaborate on a shared vault with someone else, and priority support.

For a single person who just wants their notes on two devices, that’s $48 a year on the annual rate: a real, recurring cost for what many other apps in this category treat as a baseline feature rather than an upsell.

## Publish: for putting a vault on the public web

Publish is a different add-on again, aimed at people who want to turn some or all of a vault into a website, a public wiki, documentation, or a digital garden. It costs $8 a month per site billed annually, or $10 a month billed monthly, and includes a customisable theme, graph view and full-text search on the published site, with no separate hosting to arrange.

This one is genuinely optional for most people: if you’re not planning to publish notes publicly, you will never need it.

## Catalyst and Commercial: optional, not required for work use

Catalyst is a one-off $25 payment, not a subscription. It funds development ahead of general release and gets you early access to beta builds and some community extras. It doesn’t unlock Sync or Publish, and it isn’t required to use anything in the free app.

Commercial licence is $50 per user, per year, and it’s aimed at organisations that want to support development, not a requirement for using the app at work. Obsidian’s own licence page states plainly that the free app is free for all purposes, including commercial use, non-profits, schools and government bodies, no account or payment required. Buying a Commercial licence gets an organisation listed as a supporter; it doesn’t unlock anything the free app can’t already do. Students, faculty and nonprofit employees separately get 40% off Sync and Publish.

## What it actually costs, for the sizes people actually are

- One person, one device, notes only: free, indefinitely, no catch.
- One person, two or more devices: $48 a year for Sync (annual rate), or $60 a year paying monthly.
- One person who also wants to publish a note publicly: add Publish on top: $96 a year annually, or $120 monthly, for $144 a year total alongside Sync.
- A small team sharing a vault, at work: Sync per seat if you want cross-device syncing, same as anyone else. A Commercial licence ($50 a year per seat) is optional, there to support development, not a requirement for using Obsidian in a business.

The pattern to notice: the number on Obsidian’s homepage is the true price for the app itself, but the thing most people actually need it to do – follow them between devices – is priced separately, and isn’t obvious until you go looking for it.

title: Is Obsidian Worth It in 2026? Free App, Sync and Publish
text:
## The quick answer

Obsidian is free to use, including for work, and its optional Sync starts at $4 per user per month billed annually or $5 billed monthly, as listed on October 19, 2026. Publish, the hosted-site add-on, is $8 per site per month billed annually or $10 billed monthly. Catalyst is a $25 one-time payment and the Commercial license is $50 per user per year, and Obsidian lists both as optional. Sync Standard caps files at 5 MB, and students, faculty members and nonprofit employees get 40% off Sync and Publish. For shared team documents, see our Notion AI review.

...

The Obsidian app is free, so the useful question is which paid add-on, if any, earns its price. Obsidian's pricing page calls the app "Free without limits" with no sign-up required, and its license overview says it is free for personal, commercial, non-profit, educational and government use. Spending starts when you add Sync, Publish or an optional license.

...

## Obsidian prices at a glance

Dollar prices read October 19, 2026 on Obsidian's pricing, Sync and Publish pages. The pricing page shows one Sync card at the Standard rate; Sync Plus is on the Sync page.

| Product | Unit | Billed yearly | Billed monthly | What it covers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Obsidian app | No billing | $0 | $0 | Free without limits, no sign-up required, free for commercial use |
| Sync Standard | Per user, per month | $4 | $5 | 1 vault, 1 GB storage, 5 MB maximum file size, 1 month version history |
| Sync Plus | Per user, per month | $8 | $10 | 10 vaults, 10 GB storage (upgradable to 100 GB), 200 MB maximum file size, 12 month version history |
| Publish | Per site, per month | $8 | $10 | Hosting for your site up to 4 GB, priority email support, customizable theme and domain |
| Catalyst license | One-time payment | $25 once | Not applicable | Early access to beta versions, community badges, exclusive channels |
| Commercial license | Per user, per year | $50 | Not applicable | Supports development; 25 or more licenses can earn a featured listing; does not include Sync, Publish or Catalyst |

...

##

...

- → You want notes kept as files on your own device, at $0 to start.
- → You use several devices and want Obsidian's own sync, with files under 5 MB on Standard or 200 MB on Plus.
- → You want a hosted, themed site built from your notes and accept $96 a year billed annually for one site.
- → You are a student, faculty member or nonprofit employee who can claim the 40% discount.

...

## Is Obsidian free for work, and what is the catch?

Yes. Obsidian's pricing FAQ asks "Do I have to pay for commercial use?" and answers "No. You are not required to pay for a commercial license." It encourages organizations to buy one anyway, to keep Obsidian independent and "100% user-supported." That is Obsidian's wording, not legal advice, and the license overview calls itself a simplified summary (last updated February 20, 2025), so a company with a legal team should read the terms of service it links.

The catch is that the free app leaves syncing and publishing to you. Obsidian's sync guide says that reaching your notes on a second device means choosing a sync method, and Sync and Publish are the paid options Obsidian sells.

## How much does Obsidian Sync cost?

Sync has two plans, both priced per user. Standard is the entry plan at $4 per user per month billed annually ($5 billed monthly), and Plus costs twice that on either billing term. Obsidian's pricing page shows the Standard-rate card, so Plus is easy to miss. It is on the Sync page.

The plans differ in limits. Standard allows 1 vault, 1 GB of storage, files up to 5 MB and 1 month of version history. Plus allows 10 vaults, 10 GB, files up to 200 MB and 12 months of history, with an upgrade to 100 GB that Obsidian does not price on its public pricing, Sync or plan pages. A 5 MB file cap rules Standard out for heavy attachments, and Obsidian says syncing stops when an account reaches its storage limit, which counts version history and attachments (see the plan table).

Annual billing is a small discount: $4 x 12 is $48 a year against $60 billed monthly ($5 x 12), so $12 saved on Standard and $24 on Plus. Two rules catch people late. Files sync while Obsidian is running, not in the background (see the Sync FAQ), and remote data is kept for one month after a subscription expires, while local vaults are unaffected.

...

Publish is priced per site, so one site costs $96 a year billed annually ($120 billed monthly) and two sites cost $192 billed annually. The Publish page lists hosting up to 4 GB, priority email support, a customizable theme and domain, and SEO and mobile performance.

...

## What does a year of Obsidian cost?

Take a solo knowledge worker with a laptop and a phone, over one year. Free and local costs $0, with no Obsidian sync between the devices. Adding Sync Standard costs $48 billed annually or $60 billed monthly, and one Publish site on top makes $144 billed annually ($48 + $96) or $180 billed monthly ($60 + $120). Swapping in Sync Plus doubles the Sync line on either billing term.

Students, faculty members and nonprofit employees get 40% off Sync and Publish, and Obsidian's pricing page says it offers no other discounts or promotions. You apply in your account's Billing section with an educational or organization email, approval can be instant or take up to 3 business days, and you renew the discount when it expires (see the discount page). On the annual rates that brings Standard to $28.80 a year and Standard plus one Publish site to $86.40. Obsidian prints no discounted prices, so read your checkout total before relying on that arithmetic.

A team pays per person. Obsidian says every collaborator on a shared vault needs an active Sync subscription (see Syncing for teams), and a shared vault holds up to 20 people. Five people on Standard billed annually cost $240 a year (5 x $48). The optional Commercial license for all five adds $250 (5 x $50), for $490 in total, and Obsidian says no minimum seat count applies to the Commercial license. These are list prices before any sales tax Obsidian adds at purchase (see Obsidian Credit).

title: Notion vs Obsidian for Solopreneurs: Pick by the Job (2026)
text:
Pick Notion if most of what you track has a status, a due date or a price: content calendars, launch checklists, product lists, a simple sales pipeline. Its databases and its free calendar app do that work, and the Free plan lists unlimited blocks for a single user.

Pick Obsidian if most of what you produce is writing and thinking: research notes, scripts, newsletter drafts, a long-lived idea file. Your notes stay as Markdown files in a folder on your own machine, and the app is free for business use.

If you do both kinds of work heavily, run both. Give each job one home. That last rule matters more than the choice itself.

...

The Free plan is more usable for one person than its name suggests. As of October 2026 it lists unlimited blocks for a solo user, 10 external guests, basic forms and one chart. The limits show up elsewhere: 5 MB per uploaded file and 7 days of page history. If you store video cuts, design files or big PDFs in your workspace, Free won’t hold them. Plus raises uploads to roughly 5 GB per file and history to 30 days.

...

Obsidian’s case is ownership. Your SOPs, research and drafts are text files in a folder you control, which means any backup tool, any editor and any script can work with them. For notes you expect to reread in five years, that’s the safer bet.

The licence question is settled, and plenty of older articles still get it wrong. Obsidian’s license terms, last updated February 20, 2025, say the app is free for all purposes, personal, commercial and non-profit. The $50-per-user yearly commercial license is optional, a way to support the company.

...

## What one person actually pays, October 2026

Most comparisons list plan prices without saying which ones a solo operator would actually buy. The table below prices the realistic setups for one person, collected from the official pricing and help pages on October 19, 2026.

| Setup for one person | Monthly cost | Billed yearly | The limit you’ll hit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Notion Free | $0 | $0 | 5 MB per file, 7-day page history, AI trial only |
| Notion Plus | $10 listed per member | Up to 20% off yearly | Notion AI still trial-only |
| Notion Business (for Notion AI) | $20 listed per member | Up to 20% off yearly | AI usage allowance is included, but premium models use Notion credits |
| Obsidian, no add-ons | $0 | $0 | You handle sync yourself |
| Obsidian + Sync Standard | $5 | $4/month | 1 GB total, 5 MB per file, 1 synced vault, 1 month of history |
| Obsidian + Sync Plus | $10 | $8/month | 10 GB (upgradable to 100 GB), 200 MB per file, 10 vaults, 12 months of history |
| Add Obsidian Publish | +$10 per site | +$8/month per site | One site per subscription |
| Optional Obsidian commercial license | n/a | $50 per user per year | Not required for business use |

Notion’s pricing page lists Plus at $10 and Business at $20 per member a month and says yearly billing saves up to 20%, but it doesn’t label which billing period the headline figure assumes. Check the toggle at checkout before you commit to a year.

The practical read: a solo writer on Obsidian with Sync Standard pays $48 a year. A solo operator who wants AI inside Notion pays the Business rate. Everything in between depends on whether your notes include large files.
